# Plaquette vs liasse — the corpus's two formats

The concept that reorganizes the entire pipeline architecture. Discovered by measuring the
corpus, not by reading the brief.

## The two formats

**Liasse DGFiP** — the official tax form, with a `DGFiP N° 2052` header and the
[[liasse-codes]] column. Layout fixed by law.

**Plaquette** — the presentation of the annual accounts generated by the accounting firm's
**own software** (Cegid, Sage, Quadratus, ACD…). Same figures, same conceptual order, but:

- **no two-letter codes at all**
- free-form titles: `Bilan Actif`, `Bilan Passif`, `Compte de Résultat (Première Partie)`
- extra columns the liasse doesn't have: `%`, `Variation absolue`, `Var. %`
- its own internal page numbering (`Page 5 / 67`)
- sometimes the N and N−1 columns are identified by date (`31/08/2021` / `31/08/2020`)
  instead of "Exercice N" / "Exercice N−1"

Plaquette example, `data/820561470/bilans/ocr/6493e4372f502414800f8164/page_007.json`:

```
SARL PAUTET ¦ Bilan Passif ¦ 31/08/2021. ¦ 31/08/2020 ¦
Capital social ou individuel ¦ 10 000 ¦ 10 000 ¦ Primes d'émission, de fusion, d'apport ..
```

Compare with the equivalent liasse,
`data/328024377/bilans/ocr/63e8ebbb54febda17c19ee7e/page_003.json`:

```
[267,485] Capital social ou individuel (1)* (Dont versé :   [1064,471] 152 500.
[1953,473] DA   [2161,471] 152 500
```

Same concept. One has `DA`; the other doesn't.

## The distribution across the scope

Measured across the 15 in-scope documents — see [[F001-half-the-corpus-is-not-liasse]] for
the method:

| siren | docs | format |
|---|---|---|
| `401009741` | 3 | **liasse** |
| `504304205` | 3 | **liasse** (complete, includes 2058-C) |
| `328024377` | 2 of 3 | **liasse** |
| `328024377` | 1 of 3 | plaquette |
| `445070311` | 3 | **plaquette** |
| `820561470` | 3 | **plaquette** |

**8 liasse, 7 plaquette.** The brief doesn't mention this split anywhere.

## Why this is the central architectural decision

A pipeline anchored on code covers **8 of the 15 documents** — 53%. On the other 7 it
extracts exactly zero, and has no way of knowing it failed unless you instrument it to
check.

So the pipeline needs **two distinct extractors** behind a format classifier:

```
page → format classifier
           ├── LIASSE     → code-anchored extractor   (precise, deterministic)
           └── PLAQUETTE  → label-anchored extractor  (fuzzy, needs more care)
```

And it needs a **third path** for whatever neither one resolves: escalation to a vision
model. See [[idea-05-verifier-as-router]].

## What this makes it possible to say

Scope, stated with evidence:

> *"53% of the in-scope documents are DGFiP liasses and 47% are accounting-software
> plaquettes, with no line codes. I prioritized the liasse extractor because it's
> deterministic and auditable; for the plaquettes I delivered X and left Y out. The
> classification is measured, not assumed — it's in `reports/format_classification.json`."*

The alternative — extracting "the 12 fields via the liasse codes" without having measured
this — would silently fail on half the corpus.
